task.title: Add a Next view across imported projects to the desktop app
task.description:
The merged Tasks table Workbench had is not coming back. Its use case, "across my projects, what needs my focus now?", is answered instead by a Next view: one short list per imported project, drawn from `workbook next`, so the tool's own eligibility rule decides what shows and managing each backlog is what keeps the view accurate.

## CLI first

`workbook next --limit <n>` exposes the ordered eligible set the command already walks: JSON `data` becomes `{"tasks": [...], "eligible": N}`, text prints one line per task. Plain `next` is unchanged. `--limit` with `--claim` is refused. Lands as its own PR before the desktop work.

## Desktop

- A rail entry named Next sits under the Projects header, above the project list, and renders only when two or more projects are imported. It is the launch view in that case.
- The view has one number input, "Per project" (default 1, like the Import page's Depth), and shows a group per project: priority, title, labels, assignees, age. Clicking a row opens that task on its board. A group says how many more are eligible, or that nothing is.
- No claim button, no filters, no sorting, no refresh button.
- The desktop starts every imported project's board server at launch and on import, not on first click, so each project's five-second sync loop keeps it current with origin while the app is open. The Next view polls `next --limit N --no-sync` for every project every five seconds.

Design settled 2026-09-26 with Tyler's use case: surface the choices, don't pick for the user, and keep it out of the LLM's token budget.
